title: Female upper-limb muscle attachment reference
purpose: Read-only anatomical expectation matrix for reviewing geometric proximity candidates. This dataset does not place, deform, snap, or modify meshes.
laterality: Apply left/right side matching to each donor muscle part; source references describe standard anatomy.

sources.title: Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Muscles
Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Forearm Muscles

origin.site: Anterior sternum and costal cartilages, principally ribs 1-6 (sternocostal head)

insertion.site: Lateral lip of intertubercular groove of humerus

muscles.notes: External oblique aponeurosis is also part of the described origin but is not a bone candidate.

origin.site: Anterior surfaces of ribs 3-5 near costal cartilages

muscles.notes: Some references describe anatomical variation; standard reference here uses ribs 3-5 to coracoid process.

origin.site: First rib and its costal cartilage

insertion.site: Inferior surface of middle clavicle (subclavian groove)
Costal/anterior surface of medial border of scapula

muscles.notes: The rib count can vary; the reference source describes ribs 1-8.

origin.site: Occipital region, nuchal ligament, and spinous processes C7-T12

insertion.site: Lateral clavicle, acromion, and spine of scapula

muscles.notes: Nuchal ligament is a non-bony attachment and is not represented in the bone-candidate test.

origin.site: Supraglenoid tubercle (long head) and coracoid process (short head) of scapula
Posterior humerus above/below radial groove (lateral and medial heads)
Olecranon and posterior border of ulna (ulnar head)

insertion.site: Pisiform, hook of hamate, and base of fifth metacarpal (direct/ligamentous continuity)

muscles.notes: Pisohamate and pisometacarpal ligaments transmit part of the distal attachment.

origin.site: Lateral epicondyle of humerus and posterior ulna

validationRules: A candidate appearing in the shortlist is only a geometric proximity observation, not proof of attachment.
A missing expected structure from the top-eight shortlist is inconclusive because the geometry screen is subsampled and shortlist-limited.
Compare origin and insertion independently; do not collapse them into one nearest-bone label.
Do not snap, deform, retarget, or register meshes using this reference matrix.
Laterality, tendon paths, non-bony attachments, and anatomical variants require separate review.
